title: Ahilyabai Holkar
summary: Born in 1725 in a village in Maharashtra and married into the Holkar family in 1733, Ahilyabai became ruler of Indore on 11 December 1767. She governed from Maheshwar on the Narmada until her death in 1795, and is credited with founding Maheshwar's textile industry and with building temples, ghats, wells and rest-houses.

uncertainty.note: The Press Information Bureau and Madhya Pradesh Tourism agree on birth, accession and death days; the reign is stated as 1767 to 1795.

as_recorded.value: became the ruler of Indore on December 11, 1767

where.modern_name: Maheshwar, Khargone district, Madhya Pradesh, India (pinned to her capital; she was born at Chondi, Jamkhed, Ahmednagar, Maharashtra)
where.historical_name: Maheshwar, capital of the Holkar state of Indore (Malwa) under Ahilyabai, 1767-1795

importance.justification: Ruled Malwa from 1767 to 1795 according to both sources, which describe her administration, public works and a women's unit in the army.

sources.title: Lokmata Devi Ahilyabai Holkar
sources.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India

reviewer_note: Both sources are Government of India or state tourism pages, not scholarly work. Not cross-checked against a historian's account. The pin is the Maheshwar town centre.
